item.question: In the personalization pilot, what stopped customers from ordering another personalized pair?
item.answer_markdown:
### Answer

The main stated barrier was the long wait for delivery: personalized pairs took an average of 12 days, and the lead time was the most common reason customers gave for not reordering [[NORTHSTAR/PERSO-PILOT@v1:S1.B7]][[NORTHSTAR/FY27-MEMO@v1:S1.B3]]. Customers also felt they were paying more for something that should be standard, and lacked order tracking [[NORTHSTAR/PERSO-PILOT@v1:S1.B8]].

### Key findings

- Average lead time for personalized pairs was 12 days, and 41% of exit survey respondents named the wait as their main reason not to order again [[NORTHSTAR/PERSO-PILOT@v1:S1.B7]].
- The pilot readout names the long delivery wait as the main reason people gave for not coming back [[NORTHSTAR/PERSO-PILOT@v1:S1.B2]].
- Customers praised the scan and colorway tool but commented on the waiting time, the lack of tracking, and the sense of paying more for something that should be standard [[NORTHSTAR/PERSO-PILOT@v1:S1.B8]].
- Standard delivery takes a few days, and support saw more order status questions on personalized orders [[NORTHSTAR/Q3-REVIEW@v1:SL11]].
- Personalized buyers repurchased at 18% within 90 days versus 24% for the matched control group [[NORTHSTAR/PERSO-PILOT@v1:S1.B4]].
- An interviewee abandoned an order after seeing the wait, and a reviewer nearly cancelled because the order took almost two weeks [[NORTHSTAR/PERSO-PILOT@v1:S1.B8]].

### Conflicting evidence

- An early week-six read showed personalized buyers repeating at 27%, but on a sample under 300 customers [[NORTHSTAR/Q3-REVIEW@v1:SL10.N1]].
- The final readout says that early read is superseded, with the 90-day figure at 18% against 24% for control [[NORTHSTAR/PERSO-PILOT@v1:S1.B2]][[NORTHSTAR/PERSO-PILOT@v1:S1.B4]].

### Interpretation

Lead time appears to be the dominant, but not the only, barrier, since price perception and poor order visibility were also raised [inference]. The few paid-tier takers and the preference for the free monogram suggest the price premium may also have limited appetite, though the evidence does not link this directly to non-reordering [inference].

### Gaps & unknowns

The evidence does not give the share of non-reorderers citing price, tracking, or other reasons beyond the main reason. It does not show whether shorter lead times would raise repeat purchase; a repeat test with faster delivery on a single style would help [inference]. The exit survey covered only buyers who did not reorder, so it cannot show what drove those who did reorder [inference].
